-- 0101 P6 slice J: service identities of jobs and connectors, operational exceptions with their event history and
-- stale-KPI links, and the worker heartbeat (T-DG6-ARCH-02; ADR-0053). Authored by solution-architect. Runs as
-- mth_owner inside one transaction opened by `mth-db migrate`. Forward-only: never edit once merged. SQL floor:
-- PostgreSQL 16.
--
-- REQ-S16-029 (M0330 "Avoid exposing secrets or private evidence URLs in client code or logs"; acceptance "a job's
-- identity cannot read records outside its scope") and REQ-S12-019 (M0239 "Connector/job fails or data becomes stale |
-- Create a visible operational exception and retain last known values with freshness labels").
--   service_identity           one row per job queue ('job:<queue>') or connector ('connector:<connector id>'). The
--                              DECLARATION (declared_permission_codes, sensitive_access, scope, subject) is written by a
--                              migration (jobs) or by the connector's creation (connectors) and never changed by the
--                              application afterwards; the application may only NARROW or restore the GRANT
--                              (granted_permission_codes <@ declared_permission_codes). Every code is a 'read' or
--                              'write' permission, never 'configure', 'business_approval' or 'finance_validation'
--                              (service_identity_guard). Versioned and audited; trigger-written append-only history
--                              service_identity_change. Job rows are inserted only by a migration (owner check).
--                              connector_id gets its foreign key from the connector table's migration (ADR-0055).
--   operational_exception      one ACTIVE (open or acknowledged) row per (organization, dedup key), the key being
--                              '<source_kind>:<source_code>:<failure_class>' (unique index operational_exception_one_
--                              active_key, NULLS NOT DISTINCT so platform rows are unique too). A recurrence while active
--                              increments occurrence_count by exactly 1; a recurrence after resolution opens a NEW row.
--                              States: open -> acknowledged | resolved; acknowledged -> resolved; resolved is terminal.
--                              Versioned and audited; trigger-written append-only history operational_exception_event.
--   operational_exception_kpi  append-only links from an exception to the KPI definitions whose data it makes stale
--                              (same organization; the KPI's Stale label and last value stay DG4's, ADR-0028).
--   worker_heartbeat           one row per worker instance, updated by the worker every 30 s. Operational telemetry, not
--                              a business record: version-stepped (P2 row guard) but NOT audited (the job_run precedent,
--                              0074), so a beat never writes an audit event.
-- Nothing here reads or writes DG0-DG7. No code grants a business approval.

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- service_identity
CREATE TABLE service_identity (
  id                        uuid PRIMARY KEY,
  code                      text NOT NULL CONSTRAINT service_identity_code_key UNIQUE
                              CONSTRAINT service_identity_code_format
                              CHECK (code ~ '^(job|connector):[a-z0-9][a-z0-9_.:-]{0,119}$'),
  subject_kind              text NOT NULL CHECK (subject_kind IN ('job', 'connector')),
  queue_name                text NULL CHECK (queue_name IS NULL OR (queue_name ~ '^[a-z_]+\.[a-z_.]+$'
                              AND char_length(queue_name) <= 100)),
  connector_id              uuid NULL,
  scope_level               text NOT NULL CHECK (scope_level IN ('platform', 'organization')),
  organization_id           uuid NULL REFERENCES organization (id) ON DELETE RESTRICT ON UPDATE RESTRICT,
  declared_permission_codes text[] NOT NULL CHECK (cardinality(declared_permission_codes) <= 40
                              AND array_position(declared_permission_codes, NULL) IS NULL),
  granted_permission_codes  text[] NOT NULL CHECK (array_position(granted_permission_codes, NULL) IS NULL),
  sensitive_access          text NOT NULL DEFAULT 'none' CHECK (sensitive_access IN ('none', 'aggregate_only')),
  label_en                  text NOT NULL CHECK (char_length(label_en) BETWEEN 1 AND 200),
  label_ar                  text NOT NULL CHECK (char_length(label_ar) BETWEEN 1 AND 200),
  reason                    text NOT NULL CHECK (char_length(reason) BETWEEN 3 AND 1000),
  version                   integer NOT NULL DEFAULT 1 CHECK (version >= 1),
  created_at                timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
  created_by                uuid NULL REFERENCES app_user (id) ON DELETE RESTRICT ON UPDATE RESTRICT,
  updated_at                timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
  updated_by                uuid NULL REFERENCES app_user (id) ON DELETE RESTRICT ON UPDATE RESTRICT,
  CONSTRAINT service_identity_subject_shape CHECK (
    (subject_kind = 'job' AND queue_name IS NOT NULL AND connector_id IS NULL AND code = 'job:' || queue_name)
    OR (subject_kind = 'connector' AND connector_id IS NOT NULL AND queue_name IS NULL
        AND scope_level = 'organization' AND code = 'connector:' || connector_id::text)),
  CONSTRAINT service_identity_scope_shape CHECK ((scope_level = 'platform') = (organization_id IS NULL)),
  CONSTRAINT service_identity_grant_within_declaration CHECK (granted_permission_codes <@ declared_permission_codes)
);
CREATE INDEX service_identity_organization_idx ON service_identity (organization_id, code);
SELECT p2_attach_guards('service_identity', true);
GRANT SELECT, INSERT ON service_identity TO mth_app;
-- The application can change the grant and its reason only (column privileges; probe SI).
GRANT UPDATE (granted_permission_codes, reason, version, updated_at, updated_by) ON service_identity TO mth_app;

CREATE FUNCTION service_identity_guard() RETURNS trigger
LANGUAGE plpgsql SET search_path = public, pg_temp AS $$
DECLARE
  is_owner boolean := current_user = 'mth_owner' OR current_user IN (SELECT rolname FROM pg_roles WHERE rolsuper);
  bad text;
BEGIN
  SELECT c INTO bad FROM unnest(NEW.declared_permission_codes) AS c
   WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM permission p WHERE p.code = c AND p.category IN ('read', 'write'))
   LIMIT 1;
  IF bad IS NOT NULL THEN
    RAISE EXCEPTION 'service_identity: % is not a read or write permission (a service identity never holds a configuration, business-approval or Finance-validation right)', bad
      USING ERRCODE = 'check_violation', CONSTRAINT = 'service_identity_permission_category';
  END IF;
  IF TG_OP = 'INSERT' THEN
    IF NEW.subject_kind = 'job' AND NOT is_owner THEN
      RAISE EXCEPTION 'service_identity: a job identity is declared by a migration only'
        USING ERRCODE = 'insufficient_privilege', CONSTRAINT = 'service_identity_job_by_migration';
    END IF;
    RETURN NEW;
  END IF;
  IF NOT is_owner AND (NEW.code, NEW.subject_kind, NEW.queue_name, NEW.connector_id, NEW.scope_level,
      NEW.declared_permission_codes, NEW.sensitive_access, NEW.label_en, NEW.label_ar)
     IS DISTINCT FROM (OLD.code, OLD.subject_kind, OLD.queue_name, OLD.connector_id, OLD.scope_level,
      OLD.declared_permission_codes, OLD.sensitive_access, OLD.label_en, OLD.label_ar) THEN
    RAISE EXCEPTION 'service_identity: the declaration of a service identity never changes outside a migration'
      USING ERRCODE = 'check_violation', CONSTRAINT = 'service_identity_declaration_fixed';
  END IF;
  RETURN NEW;
END $$;
CREATE TRIGGER service_identity_guard BEFORE INSERT OR UPDATE ON service_identity
  FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE FUNCTION service_identity_guard();

CREATE TABLE service_identity_change (
  id                        uuid PRIMARY KEY,
  service_identity_id       uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES service_identity (id) ON DELETE RESTRICT ON UPDATE RESTRICT,
  record_version            integer NOT NULL CHECK (record_version >= 1),
  declared_permission_codes text[] NOT NULL,
  granted_permission_codes  text[] NOT NULL,
  sensitive_access          text NOT NULL,
  reason                    text NOT NULL,
  changed_by                uuid NULL REFERENCES app_user (id) ON DELETE RESTRICT ON UPDATE RESTRICT,
  changed_at                timestamptz NOT NULL,
  CONSTRAINT service_identity_change_version_key UNIQUE (service_identity_id, record_version)
);
SELECT p2_attach_append_only('service_identity_change');
GRANT SELECT ON service_identity_change TO mth_app;

CREATE FUNCTION service_identity_history() RETURNS trigger
LANGUAGE plpgsql SECURITY DEFINER SET search_path = public, pg_temp AS $$
BEGIN
  INSERT INTO service_identity_change (id, service_identity_id, record_version, declared_permission_codes,
    granted_permission_codes, sensitive_access, reason, changed_by, changed_at)
  VALUES (mth_uuid_v7(), NEW.id, NEW.version, NEW.declared_permission_codes, NEW.granted_permission_codes,
    NEW.sensitive_access, NEW.reason, NEW.updated_by, NEW.updated_at);
  RETURN NULL;
END $$;
REVOKE ALL ON FUNCTION service_identity_history() FROM PUBLIC;
CREATE TRIGGER service_identity_history AFTER INSERT OR UPDATE ON service_identity
  FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE FUNCTION service_identity_history();

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- operational_exception
CREATE TABLE operational_exception (
  id                     uuid PRIMARY KEY,
  organization_id        uuid NULL REFERENCES organization (id) ON DELETE RESTRICT ON UPDATE RESTRICT,
  source_kind            text NOT NULL CHECK (source_kind IN ('job', 'connector', 'data_freshness', 'worker')),
  source_code            text NOT NULL CHECK (char_length(source_code) BETWEEN 1 AND 200
                           AND source_code ~ '^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9_.:-]*$'),
  failure_class          text NOT NULL CHECK (failure_class IN ('job_failed', 'connector_run_failed',
                           'connector_unreachable', 'connector_credentials_rejected', 'data_stale', 'heartbeat_missed')),
  dedup_key              text NOT NULL,
  service_identity_id    uuid NULL REFERENCES service_identity (id) ON DELETE RESTRICT ON UPDATE RESTRICT,
  operational_failure_id uuid NULL REFERENCES operational_failure (id) ON DELETE RESTRICT ON UPDATE RESTRICT,
  status                 text NOT NULL DEFAULT 'open' CHECK (status IN ('open', 'acknowledged', 'resolved')),
  occurrence_count       integer NOT NULL DEFAULT 1 CHECK (occurrence_count >= 1),
  first_occurred_at      timestamptz NOT NULL,
  last_occurred_at       timestamptz NOT NULL,
  last_error_code        text NOT NULL CHECK (char_length(last_error_code) BETWEEN 1 AND 100
                           AND last_error_code ~ '^[a-z][a-z0-9_.]*$'),
  last_error_message     text NOT NULL CHECK (char_length(last_error_message) BETWEEN 1 AND 2000),
  acknowledged_at        timestamptz NULL,
  acknowledged_by        uuid NULL REFERENCES app_user (id) ON DELETE RESTRICT ON UPDATE RESTRICT,
  acknowledge_note       text NULL CHECK (acknowledge_note IS NULL OR char_length(acknowledge_note) BETWEEN 3 AND 1000),
  resolved_at            timestamptz NULL,
  resolved_by            uuid NULL REFERENCES app_user (id) ON DELETE RESTRICT ON UPDATE RESTRICT,
  resolution             text NULL CHECK (resolution IS NULL OR resolution IN ('manual', 'recovered')),
  resolution_note        text NULL CHECK (resolution_note IS NULL OR char_length(resolution_note) BETWEEN 3 AND 1000),
  version                integer NOT NULL DEFAULT 1 CHECK (version >= 1),
  created_at             timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
  created_by             uuid NULL REFERENCES app_user (id) ON DELETE RESTRICT ON UPDATE RESTRICT,
  updated_at             timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
  updated_by             uuid NULL REFERENCES app_user (id) ON DELETE RESTRICT ON UPDATE RESTRICT,
  CONSTRAINT operational_exception_dedup_key CHECK (dedup_key = source_kind || ':' || source_code || ':' || failure_class),
  CONSTRAINT operational_exception_class_shape CHECK (
    (source_kind = 'job' AND failure_class = 'job_failed')
    OR (source_kind = 'connector' AND failure_class IN ('connector_run_failed', 'connector_unreachable',
        'connector_credentials_rejected') AND organization_id IS NOT NULL)
    OR (source_kind = 'data_freshness' AND failure_class = 'data_stale' AND organization_id IS NOT NULL)
    OR (source_kind = 'worker' AND failure_class = 'heartbeat_missed' AND organization_id IS NULL)),
  CONSTRAINT operational_exception_times CHECK (last_occurred_at >= first_occurred_at),
  CONSTRAINT operational_exception_ack_complete CHECK (
    (acknowledged_at IS NULL) = (acknowledged_by IS NULL)
    AND (acknowledge_note IS NULL OR acknowledged_at IS NOT NULL)
    AND (status <> 'acknowledged' OR acknowledged_at IS NOT NULL)
    AND (status <> 'open' OR acknowledged_at IS NULL)),
  CONSTRAINT operational_exception_resolved_complete CHECK (
    (status = 'resolved') = (resolved_at IS NOT NULL)
    AND (resolved_at IS NULL) = (resolution IS NULL)
    AND (resolution IS DISTINCT FROM 'manual' OR (resolved_by IS NOT NULL AND resolution_note IS NOT NULL))
    AND (resolution IS DISTINCT FROM 'recovered' OR resolved_by IS NULL)
    AND (resolved_at IS NOT NULL OR (resolved_by IS NULL AND resolution_note IS NULL)))
);
CREATE UNIQUE INDEX operational_exception_one_active_key ON operational_exception (organization_id, dedup_key)
  NULLS NOT DISTINCT WHERE status IN ('open', 'acknowledged');
CREATE INDEX operational_exception_list_idx ON operational_exception (organization_id, status, last_occurred_at DESC, id DESC);
SELECT p2_attach_guards('operational_exception', true);
GRANT SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE ON operational_exception TO mth_app;

CREATE FUNCTION operational_exception_guard() RETURNS trigger
LANGUAGE plpgsql SET search_path = public, pg_temp AS $$
BEGIN
  IF TG_OP = 'INSERT' THEN
    IF NEW.status <> 'open' OR NEW.occurrence_count <> 1 OR NEW.last_occurred_at <> NEW.first_occurred_at THEN
      RAISE EXCEPTION 'operational_exception: an exception is created open, with one occurrence'
        USING ERRCODE = 'check_violation', CONSTRAINT = 'operational_exception_transition';
    END IF;
    RETURN NEW;
  END IF;
  IF OLD.status = 'resolved' THEN
    RAISE EXCEPTION 'operational_exception: a resolved exception never changes (a new failure opens a new exception)'
      USING ERRCODE = 'check_violation', CONSTRAINT = 'operational_exception_resolved_final';
  END IF;
  IF (NEW.source_kind, NEW.source_code, NEW.failure_class, NEW.dedup_key, NEW.first_occurred_at)
     IS DISTINCT FROM (OLD.source_kind, OLD.source_code, OLD.failure_class, OLD.dedup_key, OLD.first_occurred_at) THEN
    RAISE EXCEPTION 'operational_exception: the source, failure class and first occurrence never change'
      USING ERRCODE = 'check_violation', CONSTRAINT = 'operational_exception_identity_fixed';
  END IF;
  IF NEW.status IS DISTINCT FROM OLD.status AND NOT (
       (OLD.status = 'open' AND NEW.status IN ('acknowledged', 'resolved'))
       OR (OLD.status = 'acknowledged' AND NEW.status = 'resolved')) THEN
    RAISE EXCEPTION 'operational_exception: % -> % is not allowed', OLD.status, NEW.status
      USING ERRCODE = 'check_violation', CONSTRAINT = 'operational_exception_transition';
  END IF;
  IF NEW.occurrence_count <> OLD.occurrence_count AND (NEW.occurrence_count <> OLD.occurrence_count + 1
       OR NEW.last_occurred_at < OLD.last_occurred_at) THEN
    RAISE EXCEPTION 'operational_exception: each recurrence counts once and moves last_occurred_at forward'
      USING ERRCODE = 'check_violation', CONSTRAINT = 'operational_exception_occurrence_step';
  END IF;
  IF NEW.occurrence_count = OLD.occurrence_count AND NEW.last_occurred_at <> OLD.last_occurred_at THEN
    RAISE EXCEPTION 'operational_exception: last_occurred_at moves only with a recurrence'
      USING ERRCODE = 'check_violation', CONSTRAINT = 'operational_exception_occurrence_step';
  END IF;
  IF OLD.acknowledged_at IS NOT NULL AND (NEW.acknowledged_at, NEW.acknowledged_by, NEW.acknowledge_note)
     IS DISTINCT FROM (OLD.acknowledged_at, OLD.acknowledged_by, OLD.acknowledge_note) THEN
    RAISE EXCEPTION 'operational_exception: an acknowledgement is recorded once'
      USING ERRCODE = 'check_violation', CONSTRAINT = 'operational_exception_ack_once';
  END IF;
  RETURN NEW;
END $$;
CREATE TRIGGER operational_exception_guard BEFORE INSERT OR UPDATE ON operational_exception
  FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE FUNCTION operational_exception_guard();

CREATE TABLE operational_exception_event (
  id                       uuid PRIMARY KEY,
  operational_exception_id uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES operational_exception (id) ON DELETE RESTRICT ON UPDATE RESTRICT,
  record_version           integer NOT NULL CHECK (record_version >= 1),
  event_kind               text NOT NULL CHECK (event_kind IN ('opened', 'recurred', 'acknowledged', 'resolved', 'updated')),
  status                   text NOT NULL,
  occurrence_count         integer NOT NULL,
  error_code               text NOT NULL,
  actor_user_id            uuid NULL REFERENCES app_user (id) ON DELETE RESTRICT ON UPDATE RESTRICT,
  note                     text NULL,
  occurred_at              timestamptz NOT NULL,
  CONSTRAINT operational_exception_event_version_key UNIQUE (operational_exception_id, record_version)
);
SELECT p2_attach_append_only('operational_exception_event');
GRANT SELECT ON operational_exception_event TO mth_app;

CREATE FUNCTION operational_exception_history() RETURNS trigger
LANGUAGE plpgsql SECURITY DEFINER SET search_path = public, pg_temp AS $$
DECLARE
  kind text;
  note text;
BEGIN
  IF TG_OP = 'INSERT' THEN
    kind := 'opened';
  ELSIF NEW.status = 'resolved' AND OLD.status <> 'resolved' THEN
    kind := 'resolved';
    note := NEW.resolution_note;
  ELSIF NEW.status = 'acknowledged' AND OLD.status = 'open' THEN
    kind := 'acknowledged';
    note := NEW.acknowledge_note;
  ELSIF NEW.occurrence_count <> OLD.occurrence_count THEN
    kind := 'recurred';
  ELSE
    kind := 'updated';
  END IF;
  INSERT INTO operational_exception_event (id, operational_exception_id, record_version, event_kind, status,
    occurrence_count, error_code, actor_user_id, note, occurred_at)
  VALUES (mth_uuid_v7(), NEW.id, NEW.version, kind, NEW.status, NEW.occurrence_count, NEW.last_error_code,
    NEW.updated_by, note, NEW.updated_at);
  RETURN NULL;
END $$;
REVOKE ALL ON FUNCTION operational_exception_history() FROM PUBLIC;
CREATE TRIGGER operational_exception_history AFTER INSERT OR UPDATE ON operational_exception
  FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE FUNCTION operational_exception_history();

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- operational_exception_kpi: which KPIs an exception makes stale (written in the exception's open/recur transaction,
-- whose audit event lists the KPI ids).
CREATE TABLE operational_exception_kpi (
  id                       uuid PRIMARY KEY,
  operational_exception_id uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES operational_exception (id) ON DELETE RESTRICT ON UPDATE RESTRICT,
  organization_id          uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES organization (id) ON DELETE RESTRICT ON UPDATE RESTRICT,
  transformation_id        uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES transformation (id) ON DELETE RESTRICT ON UPDATE RESTRICT,
  kpi_definition_id        uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES kpi_definition (id) ON DELETE RESTRICT ON UPDATE RESTRICT,
  linked_at                timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
  CONSTRAINT operational_exception_kpi_key UNIQUE (operational_exception_id, kpi_definition_id)
);
CREATE INDEX operational_exception_kpi_transformation_idx ON operational_exception_kpi (transformation_id, kpi_definition_id);
SELECT p2_attach_append_only('operational_exception_kpi');
GRANT SELECT, INSERT ON operational_exception_kpi TO mth_app;

CREATE FUNCTION operational_exception_kpi_guard() RETURNS trigger
LANGUAGE plpgsql SET search_path = public, pg_temp AS $$
BEGIN
  IF NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM kpi_definition k WHERE k.id = NEW.kpi_definition_id
                   AND k.organization_id = NEW.organization_id AND k.transformation_id = NEW.transformation_id)
     OR NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM operational_exception e WHERE e.id = NEW.operational_exception_id
                   AND e.organization_id = NEW.organization_id) THEN
    RAISE EXCEPTION 'operational_exception_kpi: the KPI and the exception must belong to the same organization (and the KPI to the named transformation)'
      USING ERRCODE = 'foreign_key_violation', CONSTRAINT = 'operational_exception_kpi_same_scope';
  END IF;
  RETURN NEW;
END $$;
CREATE TRIGGER operational_exception_kpi_guard BEFORE INSERT ON operational_exception_kpi
  FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE FUNCTION operational_exception_kpi_guard();

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- worker_heartbeat: operational telemetry (not audited, see the header).
CREATE TABLE worker_heartbeat (
  id           uuid PRIMARY KEY,
  instance_key text NOT NULL CONSTRAINT worker_heartbeat_instance_key UNIQUE
                 CHECK (instance_key ~ '^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9_.:-]{0,99}$'),
  app_version  text NOT NULL CHECK (char_length(app_version) BETWEEN 1 AND 50),
  started_at   timestamptz NOT NULL,
  last_beat_at timestamptz NOT NULL,
  beat_count   bigint NOT NULL DEFAULT 1 CHECK (beat_count >= 1),
  queue_count  integer NOT NULL CHECK (queue_count BETWEEN 0 AND 1000),
  version      integer NOT NULL DEFAULT 1 CHECK (version >= 1),
  created_at   timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
  updated_at   timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
  CONSTRAINT worker_heartbeat_times CHECK (last_beat_at >= started_at)
);
SELECT p2_attach_guards('worker_heartbeat', false);
GRANT SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE ON worker_heartbeat TO mth_app;

CREATE FUNCTION worker_heartbeat_guard() RETURNS trigger
LANGUAGE plpgsql SET search_path = public, pg_temp AS $$
BEGIN
  IF (NEW.instance_key, NEW.started_at) IS DISTINCT FROM (OLD.instance_key, OLD.started_at)
     OR NEW.last_beat_at < OLD.last_beat_at OR NEW.beat_count <> OLD.beat_count + 1 THEN
    RAISE EXCEPTION 'worker_heartbeat: a beat moves forward by exactly one (a restarted worker writes a new instance key)'
      USING ERRCODE = 'check_violation', CONSTRAINT = 'worker_heartbeat_forward';
  END IF;
  RETURN NEW;
END $$;
CREATE TRIGGER worker_heartbeat_guard BEFORE UPDATE ON worker_heartbeat
  FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE FUNCTION worker_heartbeat_guard();

-- Create a visible operational exception and retain last known values with freshness labels").
--   service_identity           one row per job queue ('job:<queue>') or connector ('connector:<connector id>'). The
--                              DECLARATION (declared_permission_codes, sensitive_access, scope, subject) is written by a
--                              migration (jobs) or by the connector's creation (connectors) and never changed by the
--                              application afterwards; the application may only NARROW or restore the GRANT
--                              (granted_permission_codes <@ declared_permission_codes). Every code is a 'read' or
--                              'write' permission, never 'configure', 'business_approval' or 'finance_validation'
--                              (service_identity_guard). Versioned and audited; trigger-written append-only history
--                              service_identity_change. Job rows are inserted only by a migration (owner check).
--                              connector_id gets its foreign key from the connector table's migration (ADR-0055).
--   operational_exception      one ACTIVE (open or acknowledged) row per (organization, dedup key), the key being
--                              '<source_kind>:<source_code>:<failure_class>' (unique index operational_exception_one_
--                              active_key, NULLS NOT DISTINCT so platform rows are unique too). A recurrence while active
--                              increments occurrence_count by exactly 1; a recurrence after resolution opens a NEW row.
--                              States: open -> acknowledged | resolved; acknowledged -> resolved; resolved is terminal.
--                              Versioned and audited; trigger-written append-only history operational_exception_event.
--   operational_exception_kpi  append-only links from an exception to the KPI definitions whose data it makes stale
--                              (same organization; the KPI's Stale label and last value stay DG4's, ADR-0028).
--   worker_heartbeat           one row per worker instance, updated by the worker every 30 s. Operational telemetry, not
--                              a business record: version-stepped (P2 row guard) but NOT audited (the job_run precedent,
--                              0074), so a beat never writes an audit event.
-- Nothing here reads or writes DG0-DG7. No code grants a business approval.

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- service_identity
CREATE TABLE service_identity (
  id                        uuid PRIMARY KEY,
  code                      text NOT NULL CONSTRAINT service_identity_code_key UNIQUE
                              CONSTRAINT service_identity_code_format
                              CHECK (code ~ '^(job|connector):[a-z0-9][a-z0-9_.:-]{0,119}$'),
  subject_kind              text NOT NULL CHECK (subject_kind IN ('job', 'connector')),
  queue_name                text NULL CHECK (queue_name IS NULL OR (queue_name ~ '^[a-z_]+\.[a-z_.]+$'
                              AND char_length(queue_name) <= 100)),
  connector_id              uuid NULL,
  scope_level               text NOT NULL CHECK (scope_level IN ('platform', 'organization')),
  organization_id           uuid NULL REFERENCES organization (id) ON DELETE RESTRICT ON UPDATE RESTRICT,
  declared_permission_codes text[] NOT NULL CHECK (cardinality(declared_permission_codes) <= 40
                              AND array_position(declared_permission_codes, NULL) IS NULL),
  granted_permission_codes  text[] NOT NULL CHECK (array_position(granted_permission_codes, NULL) IS NULL),
  sensitive_access          text NOT NULL DEFAULT 'none' CHECK (sensitive_access IN ('none', 'aggregate_only')),
  label_en                  text NOT NULL CHECK (char_length(label_en) BETWEEN 1 AND 200),
  label_ar                  text NOT NULL CHECK (char_length(label_ar) BETWEEN 1 AND 200),
  reason                    text NOT NULL CHECK (char_length(reason) BETWEEN 3 AND 1000),
  version                   integer NOT NULL DEFAULT 1 CHECK (version >= 1),
  created_at                timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
  created_by                uuid NULL REFERENCES app_user (id) ON DELETE RESTRICT ON UPDATE RESTRICT,
  updated_at                timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
  updated_by                uuid NULL REFERENCES app_user (id) ON DELETE RESTRICT ON UPDATE RESTRICT,
  CONSTRAINT service_identity_subject_shape CHECK (
    (subject_kind = 'job' AND queue_name IS NOT NULL AND connector_id IS NULL AND code = 'job:' || queue_name)
    OR (subject_kind = 'connector' AND connector_id IS NOT NULL AND queue_name IS NULL
        AND scope_level = 'organization' AND code = 'connector:' || connector_id::text)),
  CONSTRAINT service_identity_scope_shape CHECK ((scope_level = 'platform') = (organization_id IS NULL)),
  CONSTRAINT service_identity_grant_within_declaration CHECK (granted_permission_codes <@ declared_permission_codes)
);
CREATE INDEX service_identity_organization_idx ON service_identity (organization_id, code);
SELECT p2_attach_guards('service_identity', true);
GRANT SELECT, INSERT ON service_identity TO mth_app;
-- The application can change the grant and its reason only (column privileges; probe SI).
GRANT UPDATE (granted_permission_codes, reason, version, updated_at, updated_by) ON service_identity TO mth_app;

CREATE FUNCTION service_identity_guard() RETURNS trigger
LANGUAGE plpgsql SET search_path = public, pg_temp AS $$
DECLARE
  is_owner boolean := current_user = 'mth_owner' OR current_user IN (SELECT rolname FROM pg_roles WHERE rolsuper);
  bad text;
BEGIN
  SELECT c INTO bad FROM unnest(NEW.declared_permission_codes) AS c
   WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM permission p WHERE p.code = c AND p.category IN ('read', 'write'))
   LIMIT 1;
  IF bad IS NOT NULL THEN
    RAISE EXCEPTION 'service_identity: % is not a read or write permission (a service identity never holds a configuration, business-approval or Finance-validation right)', bad
      USING ERRCODE = 'check_violation', CONSTRAINT = 'service_identity_permission_category';
  END IF;
  IF TG_OP = 'INSERT' THEN
    IF NEW.subject_kind = 'job' AND NOT is_owner THEN
      RAISE EXCEPTION 'service_identity: a job identity is declared by a migration only'
        USING ERRCODE = 'insufficient_privilege', CONSTRAINT = 'service_identity_job_by_migration';
    END IF;
    RETURN NEW;
  END IF;
  IF NOT is_owner AND (NEW.code, NEW.subject_kind, NEW.queue_name, NEW.connector_id, NEW.scope_level,
      NEW.declared_permission_codes, NEW.sensitive_access, NEW.label_en, NEW.label_ar)
     IS DISTINCT FROM (OLD.code, OLD.subject_kind, OLD.queue_name, OLD.connector_id, OLD.scope_level,
      OLD.declared_permission_codes, OLD.sensitive_access, OLD.label_en, OLD.label_ar) THEN
    RAISE EXCEPTION 'service_identity: the declaration of a service identity never changes outside a migration'
      USING ERRCODE = 'check_violation', CONSTRAINT = 'service_identity_declaration_fixed';
  END IF;
  RETURN NEW;
END $$;
CREATE TRIGGER service_identity_guard BEFORE INSERT OR UPDATE ON service_identity
  FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE FUNCTION service_identity_guard();

CREATE TABLE service_identity_change (
  id                        uuid PRIMARY KEY,
  service_identity_id       uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES service_identity (id) ON DELETE RESTRICT ON UPDATE RESTRICT,
  record_version            integer NOT NULL CHECK (record_version >= 1),
  declared_permission_codes text[] NOT NULL,
  granted_permission_codes  text[] NOT NULL,
  sensitive_access          text NOT NULL,
  reason                    text NOT NULL,
  changed_by                uuid NULL REFERENCES app_user (id) ON DELETE RESTRICT ON UPDATE RESTRICT,
  changed_at                timestamptz NOT NULL,
  CONSTRAINT service_identity_change_version_key UNIQUE (service_identity_id, record_version)
);
SELECT p2_attach_append_only('service_identity_change');
GRANT SELECT ON service_identity_change TO mth_app;

CREATE FUNCTION service_identity_history() RETURNS trigger
LANGUAGE plpgsql SECURITY DEFINER SET search_path = public, pg_temp AS $$
BEGIN
  INSERT INTO service_identity_change (id, service_identity_id, record_version, declared_permission_codes,
    granted_permission_codes, sensitive_access, reason, changed_by, changed_at)
  VALUES (mth_uuid_v7(), NEW.id, NEW.version, NEW.declared_permission_codes, NEW.granted_permission_codes,
    NEW.sensitive_access, NEW.reason, NEW.updated_by, NEW.updated_at);
  RETURN NULL;
END $$;
REVOKE ALL ON FUNCTION service_identity_history() FROM PUBLIC;
CREATE TRIGGER service_identity_history AFTER INSERT OR UPDATE ON service_identity
  FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE FUNCTION service_identity_history();

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- operational_exception
CREATE TABLE operational_exception (
  id                     uuid PRIMARY KEY,
  organization_id        uuid NULL REFERENCES organization (id) ON DELETE RESTRICT ON UPDATE RESTRICT,
  source_kind            text NOT NULL CHECK (source_kind IN ('job', 'connector', 'data_freshness', 'worker')),
  source_code            text NOT NULL CHECK (char_length(source_code) BETWEEN 1 AND 200
                           AND source_code ~ '^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9_.:-]*$'),
  failure_class          text NOT NULL CHECK (failure_class IN ('job_failed', 'connector_run_failed',
                           'connector_unreachable', 'connector_credentials_rejected', 'data_stale', 'heartbeat_missed')),
  dedup_key              text NOT NULL,
  service_identity_id    uuid NULL REFERENCES service_identity (id) ON DELETE RESTRICT ON UPDATE RESTRICT,
  operational_failure_id uuid NULL REFERENCES operational_failure (id) ON DELETE RESTRICT ON UPDATE RESTRICT,
  status                 text NOT NULL DEFAULT 'open' CHECK (status IN ('open', 'acknowledged', 'resolved')),
  occurrence_count       integer NOT NULL DEFAULT 1 CHECK (occurrence_count >= 1),
  first_occurred_at      timestamptz NOT NULL,
  last_occurred_at       timestamptz NOT NULL,
  last_error_code        text NOT NULL CHECK (char_length(last_error_code) BETWEEN 1 AND 100
                           AND last_error_code ~ '^[a-z][a-z0-9_.]*$'),
  last_error_message     text NOT NULL CHECK (char_length(last_error_message) BETWEEN 1 AND 2000),
  acknowledged_at        timestamptz NULL,
  acknowledged_by        uuid NULL REFERENCES app_user (id) ON DELETE RESTRICT ON UPDATE RESTRICT,
  acknowledge_note       text NULL CHECK (acknowledge_note IS NULL OR char_length(acknowledge_note) BETWEEN 3 AND 1000),
  resolved_at            timestamptz NULL,
  resolved_by            uuid NULL REFERENCES app_user (id) ON DELETE RESTRICT ON UPDATE RESTRICT,
  resolution             text NULL CHECK (resolution IS NULL OR resolution IN ('manual', 'recovered')),
  resolution_note        text NULL CHECK (resolution_note IS NULL OR char_length(resolution_note) BETWEEN 3 AND 1000),
  version                integer NOT NULL DEFAULT 1 CHECK (version >= 1),
  created_at             timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
  created_by             uuid NULL REFERENCES app_user (id) ON DELETE RESTRICT ON UPDATE RESTRICT,
  updated_at             timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
  updated_by             uuid NULL REFERENCES app_user (id) ON DELETE RESTRICT ON UPDATE RESTRICT,
  CONSTRAINT operational_exception_dedup_key CHECK (dedup_key = source_kind || ':' || source_code || ':' || failure_class),
  CONSTRAINT operational_exception_class_shape CHECK (
    (source_kind = 'job' AND failure_class = 'job_failed')
    OR (source_kind = 'connector' AND failure_class IN ('connector_run_failed', 'connector_unreachable',
        'connector_credentials_rejected') AND organization_id IS NOT NULL)
    OR (source_kind = 'data_freshness' AND failure_class = 'data_stale' AND organization_id IS NOT NULL)
    OR (source_kind = 'worker' AND failure_class = 'heartbeat_missed' AND organization_id IS NULL)),
  CONSTRAINT operational_exception_times CHECK (last_occurred_at >= first_occurred_at),
  CONSTRAINT operational_exception_ack_complete CHECK (
    (acknowledged_at IS NULL) = (acknowledged_by IS NULL)
    AND (acknowledge_note IS NULL OR acknowledged_at IS NOT NULL)
    AND (status <> 'acknowledged' OR acknowledged_at IS NOT NULL)
    AND (status <> 'open' OR acknowledged_at IS NULL)),
  CONSTRAINT operational_exception_resolved_complete CHECK (
    (status = 'resolved') = (resolved_at IS NOT NULL)
    AND (resolved_at IS NULL) = (resolution IS NULL)
    AND (resolution IS DISTINCT FROM 'manual' OR (resolved_by IS NOT NULL AND resolution_note IS NOT NULL))
    AND (resolution IS DISTINCT FROM 'recovered' OR resolved_by IS NULL)
    AND (resolved_at IS NOT NULL OR (resolved_by IS NULL AND resolution_note IS NULL)))
);
CREATE UNIQUE INDEX operational_exception_one_active_key ON operational_exception (organization_id, dedup_key)
  NULLS NOT DISTINCT WHERE status IN ('open', 'acknowledged');
CREATE INDEX operational_exception_list_idx ON operational_exception (organization_id, status, last_occurred_at DESC, id DESC);
SELECT p2_attach_guards('operational_exception', true);
GRANT SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE ON operational_exception TO mth_app;

CREATE FUNCTION operational_exception_guard() RETURNS trigger
LANGUAGE plpgsql SET search_path = public, pg_temp AS $$
BEGIN
  IF TG_OP = 'INSERT' THEN
    IF NEW.status <> 'open' OR NEW.occurrence_count <> 1 OR NEW.last_occurred_at <> NEW.first_occurred_at THEN
      RAISE EXCEPTION 'operational_exception: an exception is created open, with one occurrence'
        USING ERRCODE = 'check_violation', CONSTRAINT = 'operational_exception_transition';
    END IF;
    RETURN NEW;
  END IF;
  IF OLD.status = 'resolved' THEN
    RAISE EXCEPTION 'operational_exception: a resolved exception never changes (a new failure opens a new exception)'
      USING ERRCODE = 'check_violation', CONSTRAINT = 'operational_exception_resolved_final';
  END IF;
  IF (NEW.source_kind, NEW.source_code, NEW.failure_class, NEW.dedup_key, NEW.first_occurred_at)
     IS DISTINCT FROM (OLD.source_kind, OLD.source_code, OLD.failure_class, OLD.dedup_key, OLD.first_occurred_at) THEN
    RAISE EXCEPTION 'operational_exception: the source, failure class and first occurrence never change'
      USING ERRCODE = 'check_violation', CONSTRAINT = 'operational_exception_identity_fixed';
  END IF;
  IF NEW.status IS DISTINCT FROM OLD.status AND NOT (
       (OLD.status = 'open' AND NEW.status IN ('acknowledged', 'resolved'))
       OR (OLD.status = 'acknowledged' AND NEW.status = 'resolved')) THEN
    RAISE EXCEPTION 'operational_exception: % -> % is not allowed', OLD.status, NEW.status
      USING ERRCODE = 'check_violation', CONSTRAINT = 'operational_exception_transition';
  END IF;
  IF NEW.occurrence_count <> OLD.occurrence_count AND (NEW.occurrence_count <> OLD.occurrence_count + 1
       OR NEW.last_occurred_at < OLD.last_occurred_at) THEN
    RAISE EXCEPTION 'operational_exception: each recurrence counts once and moves last_occurred_at forward'
      USING ERRCODE = 'check_violation', CONSTRAINT = 'operational_exception_occurrence_step';
  END IF;
  IF NEW.occurrence_count = OLD.occurrence_count AND NEW.last_occurred_at <> OLD.last_occurred_at THEN
    RAISE EXCEPTION 'operational_exception: last_occurred_at moves only with a recurrence'
      USING ERRCODE = 'check_violation', CONSTRAINT = 'operational_exception_occurrence_step';
  END IF;
  IF OLD.acknowledged_at IS NOT NULL AND (NEW.acknowledged_at, NEW.acknowledged_by, NEW.acknowledge_note)
     IS DISTINCT FROM (OLD.acknowledged_at, OLD.acknowledged_by, OLD.acknowledge_note) THEN
    RAISE EXCEPTION 'operational_exception: an acknowledgement is recorded once'
      USING ERRCODE = 'check_violation', CONSTRAINT = 'operational_exception_ack_once';
  END IF;
  RETURN NEW;
END $$;
CREATE TRIGGER operational_exception_guard BEFORE INSERT OR UPDATE ON operational_exception
  FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE FUNCTION operational_exception_guard();

CREATE TABLE operational_exception_event (
  id                       uuid PRIMARY KEY,
  operational_exception_id uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES operational_exception (id) ON DELETE RESTRICT ON UPDATE RESTRICT,
  record_version           integer NOT NULL CHECK (record_version >= 1),
  event_kind               text NOT NULL CHECK (event_kind IN ('opened', 'recurred', 'acknowledged', 'resolved', 'updated')),
  status                   text NOT NULL,
  occurrence_count         integer NOT NULL,
  error_code               text NOT NULL,
  actor_user_id            uuid NULL REFERENCES app_user (id) ON DELETE RESTRICT ON UPDATE RESTRICT,
  note                     text NULL,
  occurred_at              timestamptz NOT NULL,
  CONSTRAINT operational_exception_event_version_key UNIQUE (operational_exception_id, record_version)
);
SELECT p2_attach_append_only('operational_exception_event');
GRANT SELECT ON operational_exception_event TO mth_app;

CREATE FUNCTION operational_exception_history() RETURNS trigger
LANGUAGE plpgsql SECURITY DEFINER SET search_path = public, pg_temp AS $$
DECLARE
  kind text;
  note text;
BEGIN
  IF TG_OP = 'INSERT' THEN
    kind := 'opened';
  ELSIF NEW.status = 'resolved' AND OLD.status <> 'resolved' THEN
    kind := 'resolved';
    note := NEW.resolution_note;
  ELSIF NEW.status = 'acknowledged' AND OLD.status = 'open' THEN
    kind := 'acknowledged';
    note := NEW.acknowledge_note;
  ELSIF NEW.occurrence_count <> OLD.occurrence_count THEN
    kind := 'recurred';
  ELSE
    kind := 'updated';
  END IF;
  INSERT INTO operational_exception_event (id, operational_exception_id, record_version, event_kind, status,
    occurrence_count, error_code, actor_user_id, note, occurred_at)
  VALUES (mth_uuid_v7(), NEW.id, NEW.version, kind, NEW.status, NEW.occurrence_count, NEW.last_error_code,
    NEW.updated_by, note, NEW.updated_at);
  RETURN NULL;
END $$;
REVOKE ALL ON FUNCTION operational_exception_history() FROM PUBLIC;
CREATE TRIGGER operational_exception_history AFTER INSERT OR UPDATE ON operational_exception
  FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE FUNCTION operational_exception_history();

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- operational_exception_kpi: which KPIs an exception makes stale (written in the exception's open/recur transaction,
-- whose audit event lists the KPI ids).
CREATE TABLE operational_exception_kpi (
  id                       uuid PRIMARY KEY,
  operational_exception_id uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES operational_exception (id) ON DELETE RESTRICT ON UPDATE RESTRICT,
  organization_id          uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES organization (id) ON DELETE RESTRICT ON UPDATE RESTRICT,
  transformation_id        uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES transformation (id) ON DELETE RESTRICT ON UPDATE RESTRICT,
  kpi_definition_id        uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES kpi_definition (id) ON DELETE RESTRICT ON UPDATE RESTRICT,
  linked_at                timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
  CONSTRAINT operational_exception_kpi_key UNIQUE (operational_exception_id, kpi_definition_id)
);
CREATE INDEX operational_exception_kpi_transformation_idx ON operational_exception_kpi (transformation_id, kpi_definition_id);
SELECT p2_attach_append_only('operational_exception_kpi');
GRANT SELECT, INSERT ON operational_exception_kpi TO mth_app;

CREATE FUNCTION operational_exception_kpi_guard() RETURNS trigger
LANGUAGE plpgsql SET search_path = public, pg_temp AS $$
BEGIN
  IF NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM kpi_definition k WHERE k.id = NEW.kpi_definition_id
                   AND k.organization_id = NEW.organization_id AND k.transformation_id = NEW.transformation_id)
     OR NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM operational_exception e WHERE e.id = NEW.operational_exception_id
                   AND e.organization_id = NEW.organization_id) THEN
    RAISE EXCEPTION 'operational_exception_kpi: the KPI and the exception must belong to the same organization (and the KPI to the named transformation)'
      USING ERRCODE = 'foreign_key_violation', CONSTRAINT = 'operational_exception_kpi_same_scope';
  END IF;
  RETURN NEW;
END $$;
CREATE TRIGGER operational_exception_kpi_guard BEFORE INSERT ON operational_exception_kpi
  FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE FUNCTION operational_exception_kpi_guard();

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- worker_heartbeat: operational telemetry (not audited, see the header).
CREATE TABLE worker_heartbeat (
  id           uuid PRIMARY KEY,
  instance_key text NOT NULL CONSTRAINT worker_heartbeat_instance_key UNIQUE
                 CHECK (instance_key ~ '^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9_.:-]{0,99}$'),
  app_version  text NOT NULL CHECK (char_length(app_version) BETWEEN 1 AND 50),
  started_at   timestamptz NOT NULL,
  last_beat_at timestamptz NOT NULL,
  beat_count   bigint NOT NULL DEFAULT 1 CHECK (beat_count >= 1),
  queue_count  integer NOT NULL CHECK (queue_count BETWEEN 0 AND 1000),
  version      integer NOT NULL DEFAULT 1 CHECK (version >= 1),
  created_at   timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
  updated_at   timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
  CONSTRAINT worker_heartbeat_times CHECK (last_beat_at >= started_at)
);
SELECT p2_attach_guards('worker_heartbeat', false);
GRANT SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE ON worker_heartbeat TO mth_app;

CREATE FUNCTION worker_heartbeat_guard() RETURNS trigger
LANGUAGE plpgsql SET search_path = public, pg_temp AS $$
BEGIN
  IF (NEW.instance_key, NEW.started_at) IS DISTINCT FROM (OLD.instance_key, OLD.started_at)
     OR NEW.last_beat_at < OLD.last_beat_at OR NEW.beat_count <> OLD.beat_count + 1 THEN
    RAISE EXCEPTION 'worker_heartbeat: a beat moves forward by exactly one (a restarted worker writes a new instance key)'
      USING ERRCODE = 'check_violation', CONSTRAINT = 'worker_heartbeat_forward';
  END IF;
  RETURN NEW;
END $$;
CREATE TRIGGER worker_heartbeat_guard BEFORE UPDATE ON worker_heartbeat
  FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE FUNCTION worker_heartbeat_guard();

-- 0102 P6 slice C: the evidence-storage setting, the store of each evidence file, notification channels and their
-- per-notification deliveries (T-DG6-ARCH-02; ADR-0054). Authored by solution-architect. Runs as mth_owner inside one
-- transaction opened by `mth-db migrate`. Forward-only: never edit once merged. SQL floor: PostgreSQL 16.
--
-- REQ-S16-006 (M0311 "Provide an evidence-storage adapter with a private filesystem option and an optional
-- IT-approved object-store adapter"; acceptance "contract tests pass for both adapters; evidence is never served from a
-- public URL") and REQ-S12-023 (M0241 "Always provide an in-app inbox. Email and enterprise messaging are optional
-- IT-configured adapters; their absence must not break workflows").
--   p6_secret_ref_valid(jsonb)  a SecretRef ({"provider", "name"}, ADR-0052 §5) has exactly those two keys and never a
--                               value. Credentials are stored ONLY as references.
--   storage_setting             at most one row for the installation (singleton). No row = the environment default of
--                               ADR-0010/ADR-0011 (EVIDENCE_STORAGE_DRIVER, filesystem in every shipped profile). With
--                               driver 's3' the endpoint, region, bucket and both credential references are required.
--                               Versioned and audited; trigger-written append-only history storage_setting_change.
--   evidence_content            one column storage_driver (which store holds the bytes). Every row stored before P6 is
--                               'filesystem' (the column default), so a driver change never strands an earlier file:
--                               reads use the row's driver, new writes use the current setting.
--   notification_channel        at most one row per (organization, channel kind). 'email' can be enabled when its SMTP
--                               host, port, security and sender are set; 'enterprise_messaging' has a port and no
--                               adapter in P6, so it can never be enabled. No row or a disabled row = in-app only.
--                               Versioned and audited; trigger-written append-only history notification_channel_change.
--   notification_delivery       one row per (inbox notification, channel kind): the idempotency backstop of the
--                               fan-out (UNIQUE). States: pending -> sent | failed | skipped; failed -> pending (a retry,
--                               attempts + 1 on the next attempt). sent and skipped are terminal. No message body is
--                               stored; the channel renders it from the notification at send time. Versioned and
--                               audited (service actor).
-- Nothing here reads or writes DG0-DG7.

CREATE FUNCTION p6_secret_ref_valid(r jsonb) RETURNS boolean
LANGUAGE sql IMMUTABLE PARALLEL SAFE SET search_path = pg_catalog, pg_temp AS $$
  SELECT r IS NULL OR (
    jsonb_typeof(r) = 'object'
    AND (SELECT array_agg(k ORDER BY k) FROM jsonb_object_keys(r) AS k) = ARRAY['name', 'provider']
    AND jsonb_typeof(r->'provider') = 'string' AND (r->>'provider') ~ '^[a-z][a-z0-9_]{0,31}$'
    AND jsonb_typeof(r->'name') = 'string' AND (r->>'name') ~ '^[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_./-]{0,127}$')
$$;
COMMENT ON FUNCTION p6_secret_ref_valid(jsonb) IS
  'A SecretRef {provider, name} (ADR-0052 §5): exactly two string keys, never a secret value (ADR-0054 §2).';
GRANT EXECUTE ON FUNCTION p6_secret_ref_valid(jsonb) TO mth_app;

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- storage_setting
CREATE TABLE storage_setting (
  id                  uuid PRIMARY KEY,
  singleton           boolean NOT NULL DEFAULT true CONSTRAINT storage_setting_singleton_key UNIQUE
                        CONSTRAINT storage_setting_singleton CHECK (singleton),
  driver              text NOT NULL CHECK (driver IN ('filesystem', 's3')),
  s3_endpoint         text NULL CHECK (s3_endpoint IS NULL OR (s3_endpoint ~ '^https?://[^/?#@[:space:]]+(:[0-9]{1,5})?/?$'
                        AND char_length(s3_endpoint) <= 300)),
  s3_region           text NULL CHECK (s3_region IS NULL OR s3_region ~ '^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{0,62}$'),
  s3_bucket           text NULL CHECK (s3_bucket IS NULL OR s3_bucket ~ '^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9.-]{1,61}[a-z0-9]$'),
  s3_key_prefix       text NULL CHECK (s3_key_prefix IS NULL OR s3_key_prefix ~ '^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9_/-]{0,99}$'),
  s3_force_path_style boolean NOT NULL DEFAULT true,
  s3_access_key_ref   jsonb NULL CONSTRAINT storage_setting_access_key_ref CHECK (p6_secret_ref_valid(s3_access_key_ref)),
  s3_secret_key_ref   jsonb NULL CONSTRAINT storage_setting_secret_key_ref CHECK (p6_secret_ref_valid(s3_secret_key_ref)),
  reason              text NOT NULL CHECK (char_length(reason) BETWEEN 3 AND 1000),
  version             integer NOT NULL DEFAULT 1 CHECK (version >= 1),
  created_at          timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
  created_by          uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES app_user (id) ON DELETE RESTRICT ON UPDATE RESTRICT,
  updated_at          timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
  updated_by          uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES app_user (id) ON DELETE RESTRICT ON UPDATE RESTRICT,
  CONSTRAINT storage_setting_s3_complete CHECK (driver <> 's3' OR (s3_endpoint IS NOT NULL AND s3_region IS NOT NULL
    AND s3_bucket IS NOT NULL AND s3_access_key_ref IS NOT NULL AND s3_secret_key_ref IS NOT NULL))
);
SELECT p2_attach_guards('storage_setting', true);
GRANT SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE ON storage_setting TO mth_app;

CREATE TABLE storage_setting_change (
  id                  uuid PRIMARY KEY,
  storage_setting_id  uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES storage_setting (id) ON DELETE RESTRICT ON UPDATE RESTRICT,
  record_version      integer NOT NULL CHECK (record_version >= 1),
  driver              text NOT NULL,
  s3_endpoint         text NULL,
  s3_region           text NULL,
  s3_bucket           text NULL,
  s3_key_prefix       text NULL,
  s3_force_path_style boolean NOT NULL,
  s3_access_key_ref   jsonb NULL,
  s3_secret_key_ref   jsonb NULL,
  reason              text NOT NULL,
  changed_by          uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES app_user (id) ON DELETE RESTRICT ON UPDATE RESTRICT,
  changed_at          timestamptz NOT NULL,
  CONSTRAINT storage_setting_change_version_key UNIQUE (storage_setting_id, record_version)
);
SELECT p2_attach_append_only('storage_setting_change');
GRANT SELECT ON storage_setting_change TO mth_app;

CREATE FUNCTION storage_setting_history() RETURNS trigger
LANGUAGE plpgsql SECURITY DEFINER SET search_path = public, pg_temp AS $$
BEGIN
  INSERT INTO storage_setting_change (id, storage_setting_id, record_version, driver, s3_endpoint, s3_region, s3_bucket,
    s3_key_prefix, s3_force_path_style, s3_access_key_ref, s3_secret_key_ref, reason, changed_by, changed_at)
  VALUES (mth_uuid_v7(), NEW.id, NEW.version, NEW.driver, NEW.s3_endpoint, NEW.s3_region, NEW.s3_bucket,
    NEW.s3_key_prefix, NEW.s3_force_path_style, NEW.s3_access_key_ref, NEW.s3_secret_key_ref, NEW.reason,
    NEW.updated_by, NEW.updated_at);
  RETURN NULL;
END $$;
REVOKE ALL ON FUNCTION storage_setting_history() FROM PUBLIC;
CREATE TRIGGER storage_setting_history AFTER INSERT OR UPDATE ON storage_setting
  FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE FUNCTION storage_setting_history();

ALTER TABLE evidence_content
  ADD COLUMN storage_driver text NOT NULL DEFAULT 'filesystem'
    CONSTRAINT evidence_content_storage_driver CHECK (storage_driver IN ('filesystem', 's3'));

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- notification_channel
CREATE TABLE notification_channel (
  id                uuid PRIMARY KEY,
  organization_id   uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES organization (id) ON DELETE RESTRICT ON UPDATE RESTRICT,
  channel_kind      text NOT NULL CHECK (channel_kind IN ('email', 'enterprise_messaging')),
  enabled           boolean NOT NULL DEFAULT false,
  smtp_host         text NULL CHECK (smtp_host IS NULL OR smtp_host ~ '^[A-Za-z0-9]([A-Za-z0-9.-]{0,251}[A-Za-z0-9])?$'),
  smtp_port         integer NULL CHECK (smtp_port IS NULL OR smtp_port BETWEEN 1 AND 65535),
  smtp_security     text NULL CHECK (smtp_security IS NULL OR smtp_security IN ('starttls', 'tls', 'none')),
  smtp_username_ref jsonb NULL CONSTRAINT notification_channel_username_ref CHECK (p6_secret_ref_valid(smtp_username_ref)),
  smtp_password_ref jsonb NULL CONSTRAINT notification_channel_password_ref CHECK (p6_secret_ref_valid(smtp_password_ref)),
  from_address      text NULL CHECK (from_address IS NULL OR (char_length(from_address) <= 254
                      AND from_address ~ '^[^@[:space:]<>]+@[^@[:space:]<>]+\.[^@[:space:]<>]+$')),
  reason            text NOT NULL CHECK (char_length(reason) BETWEEN 3 AND 1000),
----
-- 0103 P6 slices J and C seeds: the operations, service-identity, identity, storage and notification-channel permission
-- catalogue and its role defaults (T-DG6-ARCH-02; ADR-0053 §9, ADR-0054 §5). Authored by solution-architect. Runs as
-- mth_owner inside one transaction opened by `mth-db migrate`. Forward-only: never edit once merged. SQL floor:
-- PostgreSQL 16.
--
-- Permissions: EXACTLY packages/shared/src/permissions.ts P6_OPERATIONS_CHANNELS_PERMISSIONS /
-- P6_OPERATIONS_CHANNELS_ROLE_PERMISSIONS (packages/db/src/seed.test.ts compares them). A CONFIGURABLE STARTING POINT,
-- not a Mobily-approved access policy.
--   operations.read                read Administration > Operations: operational exceptions, the worker heartbeat and
--                                  the service identities (REQ-S12-019 "An exception is shown to admins and data
--                                  owners"): ADM_TECH, TO, KDS, TD and AUD.
--   operations.acknowledge         acknowledge or resolve an operational exception: ADM_TECH and KDS.
--   service_identity.configure     narrow or restore the permissions granted to a job's or connector's service identity
--                                  (REQ-S16-029 "configure:ADM(IT)"): ADM_TECH.
--   identity.read                  read Administration > Identity (issuer, client id, scopes, claim mapping; never the
--                                  client secret) (REQ-S16-007): ADM_TECH, ADM_ACCESS and AUD.
--   storage.configure              read, change and test the evidence-storage setting (REQ-S16-006 "configure:ADM(IT)"):
--                                  ADM_TECH.
--   notification_channel.configure read, change and test notification channels (REQ-S12-023 "configure-channels:ADM"):
--                                  ADM_TECH.
-- No code is a business_approval or finance_validation code, so the technical-admin trigger of 0001 accepts every link
-- (REQ-S10-003). AUD gets read codes only. Nothing touches DG0-DG7.
INSERT INTO permission (code, category, description_en, description_ar) VALUES
  ('operations.read', 'read', 'Read operational exceptions, the worker heartbeat and the service identities in Administration > Operations', 'قراءة الاستثناءات التشغيلية ونبض العامل وهويات الخدمة في الإدارة > العمليات'),
  ('operations.acknowledge', 'write', 'Acknowledge or resolve an operational exception', 'الإقرار باستثناء تشغيلي أو إغلاقه'),

  ('identity.read', 'read', 'Read the identity-provider settings in Administration > Identity (never the client secret)', 'قراءة إعدادات مزود الهوية في الإدارة > الهوية (دون السر الخاص بالعميل)'),
  ('storage.configure', 'configure', 'Read, change and test the evidence-storage setting', 'قراءة إعداد تخزين الأدلة وتعديله واختباره'),
  ('notification_channel.configure', 'configure', 'Read, change and test the email and enterprise-messaging notification channels', 'قراءة قنوات الإشعار عبر البريد الإلكتروني والمراسلة المؤسسية وتعديلها واختبارها');
INSERT INTO role_permission (role_id, permission_code) VALUES
  ('01920000-0000-7000-8000-000000000006', 'operations.read'), -- TO
  ('01920000-0000-7000-8000-000000000007', 'operations.read'), -- KDS
  ('01920000-0000-7000-8000-000000000007', 'operations.acknowledge'), -- KDS
  ('01920000-0000-7000-8000-000000000008', 'operations.read'), -- TD
  ('01920000-0000-7000-8000-00000000000b', 'operations.read'), -- AUD
  ('01920000-0000-7000-8000-00000000000b', 'identity.read'), -- AUD
  ('01920000-0000-7000-8000-00000000000c', 'operations.read'), -- ADM_TECH
  ('01920000-0000-7000-8000-00000000000c', 'operations.acknowledge'), -- ADM_TECH
  ('01920000-0000-7000-8000-00000000000c', 'service_identity.configure'), -- ADM_TECH
  ('01920000-0000-7000-8000-00000000000c', 'identity.read'), -- ADM_TECH

# ADR-0053: P6 operations: a constrained service identity for every job and connector, operational exceptions linked to stale KPIs, the catalogue triggers, structured logs and the redaction list, the post-suite log scan, the worker heartbeat and error alerts, and Administration > Operations

- **Status:** Proposed for P6 (DG6). Author: solution-architect (T-DG6-ARCH-02), 2026-10-26.
- **Requirements (slice J of `docs/architecture/p6-plan.md`):** REQ-S12-019, REQ-S16-029.
- **Sources (quoted where a design point has one):**
  - M0239 (§12, starter table) "Connector/job fails or data becomes stale | Create a visible operational exception; retain last known values with freshness labels".
  - M0240 (§12) "Use durable background jobs, idempotency keys, bounded retries with backoff, transaction-safe event/outbox handling and an operational failure queue. … Expose last success, next run, failures and repair actions to authorized administrators."
  - M0330 (§16) "Generated exports and search indexes must enforce the same scopes as record views. Use a constrained service identity for each connector and background job. Avoid exposing secrets or private evidence URLs in client code or logs."
  - M0331 (§16) "… a secret-management interface. Production secrets are runtime configuration, not repository content."
  - M0391 (§20, A22) "Operational readiness | Health checks, logs, error alerts, admin job visibility and production/demo separation are demonstrated". M0381 (A12) "Cross-transformation unauthorized reads/writes, exports, search results, evidence URLs and AI retrieval are denied". M0386 (A17) "… unavailable connector shows an actionable error".
  - REQ-S12-019 acceptance: "A17;A22: a failing test connector produces one exception and the KPI shows Stale with its last value and date". REQ-S16-029 acceptance: "A12;A22: a log scan after the test suite finds no secrets or storage URLs; a job's identity cannot read records outside its scope".
  - Playbook: Template 2 (B0049/B0050) gives every KPI an "Owner" column; the playbook names no operational monitoring, logging or service-identity control, so nothing below is attributed to it.
- **Decisions applied:** D-195 (Q2 evidence links, Q13 job identities enforced in the application through `ReadScope`, no PostgreSQL row-level security; Q12; R3), D-196 (migration ids), D-193, D-088 §2, D-141, F-DG3-100, F-DG4-160.
- **Builds on:** ADR-0002 rule 5 (the worker imports no API code), ADR-0004 (audit), ADR-0006 (policy), ADR-0008 (jobs, retries), ADR-0016 (P2 guards, lock registry), ADR-0025 (job kit), ADR-0028 (KPI freshness), ADR-0043 (failure queue `operational_failure`, automation service identities), ADR-0044 (starter 16 `starter.job_failed`), ADR-0051 §1 (`ReadScope`), ADR-0052 §5 (`SecretProvider`).
- **Physical model:** `packages/db/migrations/0101_p6_operations_service_identities.sql`, `0103_p6_operations_channels_permissions.sql`; probe groups SI, OE, OEK, WH, PM in `docs/delivery/handbacks/DG6/T-DG6-ARCH-02-evidence/probe-output.txt`.
- **Two gate systems.** Nothing here reads or writes DG0–DG7. A service identity never holds a business-approval or Finance-validation right. Acknowledging an exception approves nothing.

## Context

1. The 35 worker queues (`apps/worker/src/queues/**`) run through the job kit (`apps/worker/src/kit.ts`) as the audit actor `service`/`worker` with no permission and no declared read scope ("a service actor holds no permission"). Their queries are scoped by the code each handler contains, not by a declared identity. Only P5 automation actions have service identities (`automation/identity.ts`, rule-version `service_permission_codes`).
2. The failure queue `operational_failure` (`0074`, ADR-0043) holds one row per failed unit of work and key (open → retrying → resolved | open; open → dismissed). It is per job key, so 50 failing scheduled slots of one queue are 50 rows. Starter 16 (`starter.job_failed`, M0239) records them. There is no record "this source is failing" that an administrator acknowledges, and no link to the KPIs that a failing source makes stale. `grep operational_exception` finds nothing.
3. KPI freshness is computed at read time by DG4 (`kpi/kpi-status.ts`: `freshness { status: fresh | stale | unknown, dataAsOf, staleAfterDays }`, ADR-0028); the panel keeps the last accepted value. Nothing records that data became stale.
4. Logs: pino JSON, with `redact` on four paths only (`req.headers.authorization`, `req.headers.cookie`, `req.headers["x-csrf-token"]`, `res.headers["set-cookie"]`; `server.ts`). No scan checks a test run's logs.
5. The worker has no heartbeat. `/health` and `/ready` (ADR-0011) cover the API only.

## Decision

### 1. A service identity for every job queue and connector (REQ-S16-029)

**Entity `service_identity`** (`0101`): `id`, `code` (UNIQUE; `job:<queue name>` or `connector:<connector id>`), `subject_kind` (`job` | `connector`), `queue_name` (jobs), `connector_id` (connectors; its foreign key is added by ADR-0055's migration when `connector` exists), `scope_level` (`platform` | `organization`), `organization_id` (NULL iff platform), `declared_permission_codes` (the ceiling), `granted_permission_codes` (the effective grant), `sensitive_access` (`none` | `aggregate_only`), `label_en`, `label_ar`, `reason`, `version`, P2 stamps. History `service_identity_change` (trigger-written, append-only; `record_version`, both code lists, `sensitive_access`, `reason`, `changed_by`, `changed_at`).

**Database invariants (each proved by the probe):**

| # | Invariant | Mechanism | Probe |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Every declared code is a `read` or `write` permission; `configure`, `business_approval`, `finance_validation` and unknown codes are refused, also for a migration | trigger `service_identity_guard` (constraint name `service_identity_permission_category`) | SI03, SI04, SI05 |
| 2 | `granted_permission_codes ⊆ declared_permission_codes` | CHECK `service_identity_grant_within_declaration` | SI11 |
| 3 | A job identity is inserted only by a migration (role `mth_owner` or a superuser) | trigger (`service_identity_job_by_migration`, SQLSTATE 42501) | SI02 |
| 4 | The application can UPDATE only `granted_permission_codes`, `reason`, `version`, `updated_at`, `updated_by` | column-level `GRANT UPDATE (…)`; the declaration is also fixed by the trigger for non-owners (`service_identity_declaration_fixed`) | SI12 |
| 5 | `code` names its subject (`job:` + queue, `connector:` + id); a connector identity has organization scope | CHECK `service_identity_subject_shape`, `service_identity_scope_shape` | SI08, SI09 |
| 6 | Version steps by 1; every insert and update has its audit event at COMMIT; the history is append-only and not writable by the application | `p2_attach_guards(…, true)`, `p2_attach_append_only`, SELECT-only grant | SI07, SI10, SI13–SI17 |

**Who writes what.**
- **Job identities:** BE-J declares one identity per queue in code (`apps/worker/src/kit.ts`: `defineJob({ queue, identity: { permissions, scope, sensitiveAccess } })`, defaulting to the narrowest set the DG4/DG5 handler already reads) and seeds the same rows in its migration (the next id at merge, D-196). A unit test requires the code declarations and the seeded rows to be equal (the `seed.test.ts` pattern). The 35 queue names of `apps/worker/src/queues/**` at this revision are the set to declare; a queue added later declares its identity in the same change.
- **Connector identities:** created by the connector's creation (ADR-0055, BE-L) in the same transaction, with `granted = declared`.
- **Administrators** narrow or restore the grant (`putServiceIdentity`). They never widen it beyond the declaration and never change the declaration.

**How a job reads (D-195 Q13: application enforcement, no row-level security).** At the start of each run the kit loads the identity row by code and builds a service principal: the granted codes at organization scope for the organization the job names (a platform job iterates organizations and builds one principal per organization). Every business-record read of the handler goes through that principal:
- list and aggregate reads through `ReadScope` (ADR-0051 §1). ADR-0002 rule 5 forbids the worker to import `apps/api/src/modules/access/read-scope.ts`, so BE-J writes the worker twin `apps/worker/src/service-scope.ts` and a parity test against the API `ReadScope` on the ADR-0051 §1 fixture (the ADR-0043 identity-twin precedent);
- a single-record read through `requireServiceRead(principal, record)`, which throws `ServiceScopeViolation` with code `service_identity.out_of_scope` for a record outside the scope.
- **Sensitive records (ADR-0051 §2):** `sensitive_access = 'none'` excludes them like a reader without a grant. `aggregate_only` admits them **only** into aggregate computations (for example the benefit recalculation, so totals stay identical for every user, D-195 Q3) and never into a per-record output (a notification title, a work item, an export row).
- A missing identity row makes the run fail with `service_identity.missing`. A missing permission or an out-of-scope record makes it fail with `service_identity.out_of_scope`. Both are never retried (the ADR-0043 forbidden rule) and open an operational exception (§2).

**Acceptance proof (BE-J, `apps/api/test/integration/operations/service-identity-scope.test.ts`):** two organizations; for each job code that reads business records, the handler's scoped reads for organization A return no row of organization B (`ReadScope` predicate admits 0 rows), and `requireServiceRead` of an organization-B record id throws `service_identity.out_of_scope`. **Parity (P5 R2 rule):** for each touched handler, the output on the DG5 fixture is identical before and after the change (one regression test per handler).

### 2. Operational exceptions (REQ-S12-019)

**Entity `operational_exception`** (`0101`): `id`, `organization_id` (NULL for platform sources), `source_kind` (`job` | `connector` | `data_freshness` | `worker`), `source_code` (the queue name, the connector code, `kpi:<kpi definition id>`, or `worker`), `failure_class` (closed set below), `dedup_key` (= `source_kind:source_code:failure_class`, CHECK), `service_identity_id`, `operational_failure_id` (the latest failure-queue row for a job), `status`, `occurrence_count`, `first_occurred_at`, `last_occurred_at`, `last_error_code`, `last_error_message` (redacted before it is written, §4), `acknowledged_at/by`, `acknowledge_note`, `resolved_at/by`, `resolution` (`manual` | `recovered`), `resolution_note`, `version`, stamps. History `operational_exception_event` (trigger-written, append-only: `event_kind` `opened` | `recurred` | `acknowledged` | `resolved` | `updated`, status, count, error code, actor, note, time). Links `operational_exception_kpi` (append-only: exception, organization, transformation, `kpi_definition_id`, `linked_at`).

| `source_kind` | `failure_class` | Raised by | Organization |

  - Playbook: Template 2 (B0049/B0050) gives every KPI an "Owner" column; the playbook names no operational monitoring, logging or service-identity control, so nothing below is attributed to it.
- **Decisions applied:** D-195 (Q2 evidence links, Q13 job identities enforced in the application through `ReadScope`, no PostgreSQL row-level security; Q12; R3), D-196 (migration ids), D-193, D-088 §2, D-141, F-DG3-100, F-DG4-160.
- **Builds on:** ADR-0002 rule 5 (the worker imports no API code), ADR-0004 (audit), ADR-0006 (policy), ADR-0008 (jobs, retries), ADR-0016 (P2 guards, lock registry), ADR-0025 (job kit), ADR-0028 (KPI freshness), ADR-0043 (failure queue `operational_failure`, automation service identities), ADR-0044 (starter 16 `starter.job_failed`), ADR-0051 §1 (`ReadScope`), ADR-0052 §5 (`SecretProvider`).
- **Physical model:** `packages/db/migrations/0101_p6_operations_service_identities.sql`, `0103_p6_operations_channels_permissions.sql`; probe groups SI, OE, OEK, WH, PM in `docs/delivery/handbacks/DG6/T-DG6-ARCH-02-evidence/probe-output.txt`.
- **Two gate systems.** Nothing here reads or writes DG0–DG7. A service identity never holds a business-approval or Finance-validation right. Acknowledging an exception approves nothing.

## Context

1. The 35 worker queues (`apps/worker/src/queues/**`) run through the job kit (`apps/worker/src/kit.ts`) as the audit actor `service`/`worker` with no permission and no declared read scope ("a service actor holds no permission"). Their queries are scoped by the code each handler contains, not by a declared identity. Only P5 automation actions have service identities (`automation/identity.ts`, rule-version `service_permission_codes`).
2. The failure queue `operational_failure` (`0074`, ADR-0043) holds one row per failed unit of work and key (open → retrying → resolved | open; open → dismissed). It is per job key, so 50 failing scheduled slots of one queue are 50 rows. Starter 16 (`starter.job_failed`, M0239) records them. There is no record "this source is failing" that an administrator acknowledges, and no link to the KPIs that a failing source makes stale. `grep operational_exception` finds nothing.
3. KPI freshness is computed at read time by DG4 (`kpi/kpi-status.ts`: `freshness { status: fresh | stale | unknown, dataAsOf, staleAfterDays }`, ADR-0028); the panel keeps the last accepted value. Nothing records that data became stale.
4. Logs: pino JSON, with `redact` on four paths only (`req.headers.authorization`, `req.headers.cookie`, `req.headers["x-csrf-token"]`, `res.headers["set-cookie"]`; `server.ts`). No scan checks a test run's logs.
5. The worker has no heartbeat. `/health` and `/ready` (ADR-0011) cover the API only.

## Decision

### 1. A service identity for every job queue and connector (REQ-S16-029)

**Entity `service_identity`** (`0101`): `id`, `code` (UNIQUE; `job:<queue name>` or `connector:<connector id>`), `subject_kind` (`job` | `connector`), `queue_name` (jobs), `connector_id` (connectors; its foreign key is added by ADR-0055's migration when `connector` exists), `scope_level` (`platform` | `organization`), `organization_id` (NULL iff platform), `declared_permission_codes` (the ceiling), `granted_permission_codes` (the effective grant), `sensitive_access` (`none` | `aggregate_only`), `label_en`, `label_ar`, `reason`, `version`, P2 stamps. History `service_identity_change` (trigger-written, append-only; `record_version`, both code lists, `sensitive_access`, `reason`, `changed_by`, `changed_at`).

**Database invariants (each proved by the probe):**

| # | Invariant | Mechanism | Probe |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Every declared code is a `read` or `write` permission; `configure`, `business_approval`, `finance_validation` and unknown codes are refused, also for a migration | trigger `service_identity_guard` (constraint name `service_identity_permission_category`) | SI03, SI04, SI05 |
| 2 | `granted_permission_codes ⊆ declared_permission_codes` | CHECK `service_identity_grant_within_declaration` | SI11 |
| 3 | A job identity is inserted only by a migration (role `mth_owner` or a superuser) | trigger (`service_identity_job_by_migration`, SQLSTATE 42501) | SI02 |
| 4 | The application can UPDATE only `granted_permission_codes`, `reason`, `version`, `updated_at`, `updated_by` | column-level `GRANT UPDATE (…)`; the declaration is also fixed by the trigger for non-owners (`service_identity_declaration_fixed`) | SI12 |
| 5 | `code` names its subject (`job:` + queue, `connector:` + id); a connector identity has organization scope | CHECK `service_identity_subject_shape`, `service_identity_scope_shape` | SI08, SI09 |
| 6 | Version steps by 1; every insert and update has its audit event at COMMIT; the history is append-only and not writable by the application | `p2_attach_guards(…, true)`, `p2_attach_append_only`, SELECT-only grant | SI07, SI10, SI13–SI17 |

**Who writes what.**
- **Job identities:** BE-J declares one identity per queue in code (`apps/worker/src/kit.ts`: `defineJob({ queue, identity: { permissions, scope, sensitiveAccess } })`, defaulting to the narrowest set the DG4/DG5 handler already reads) and seeds the same rows in its migration (the next id at merge, D-196). A unit test requires the code declarations and the seeded rows to be equal (the `seed.test.ts` pattern). The 35 queue names of `apps/worker/src/queues/**` at this revision are the set to declare; a queue added later declares its identity in the same change.
- **Connector identities:** created by the connector's creation (ADR-0055, BE-L) in the same transaction, with `granted = declared`.
- **Administrators** narrow or restore the grant (`putServiceIdentity`). They never widen it beyond the declaration and never change the declaration.

**How a job reads (D-195 Q13: application enforcement, no row-level security).** At the start of each run the kit loads the identity row by code and builds a service principal: the granted codes at organization scope for the organization the job names (a platform job iterates organizations and builds one principal per organization). Every business-record read of the handler goes through that principal:
- list and aggregate reads through `ReadScope` (ADR-0051 §1). ADR-0002 rule 5 forbids the worker to import `apps/api/src/modules/access/read-scope.ts`, so BE-J writes the worker twin `apps/worker/src/service-scope.ts` and a parity test against the API `ReadScope` on the ADR-0051 §1 fixture (the ADR-0043 identity-twin precedent);
- a single-record read through `requireServiceRead(principal, record)`, which throws `ServiceScopeViolation` with code `service_identity.out_of_scope` for a record outside the scope.
- **Sensitive records (ADR-0051 §2):** `sensitive_access = 'none'` excludes them like a reader without a grant. `aggregate_only` admits them **only** into aggregate computations (for example the benefit recalculation, so totals stay identical for every user, D-195 Q3) and never into a per-record output (a notification title, a work item, an export row).
- A missing identity row makes the run fail with `service_identity.missing`. A missing permission or an out-of-scope record makes it fail with `service_identity.out_of_scope`. Both are never retried (the ADR-0043 forbidden rule) and open an operational exception (§2).

**Acceptance proof (BE-J, `apps/api/test/integration/operations/service-identity-scope.test.ts`):** two organizations; for each job code that reads business records, the handler's scoped reads for organization A return no row of organization B (`ReadScope` predicate admits 0 rows), and `requireServiceRead` of an organization-B record id throws `service_identity.out_of_scope`. **Parity (P5 R2 rule):** for each touched handler, the output on the DG5 fixture is identical before and after the change (one regression test per handler).

### 2. Operational exceptions (REQ-S12-019)

**Entity `operational_exception`** (`0101`): `id`, `organization_id` (NULL for platform sources), `source_kind` (`job` | `connector` | `data_freshness` | `worker`), `source_code` (the queue name, the connector code, `kpi:<kpi definition id>`, or `worker`), `failure_class` (closed set below), `dedup_key` (= `source_kind:source_code:failure_class`, CHECK), `service_identity_id`, `operational_failure_id` (the latest failure-queue row for a job), `status`, `occurrence_count`, `first_occurred_at`, `last_occurred_at`, `last_error_code`, `last_error_message` (redacted before it is written, §4), `acknowledged_at/by`, `acknowledge_note`, `resolved_at/by`, `resolution` (`manual` | `recovered`), `resolution_note`, `version`, stamps. History `operational_exception_event` (trigger-written, append-only: `event_kind` `opened` | `recurred` | `acknowledged` | `resolved` | `updated`, status, count, error code, actor, note, time). Links `operational_exception_kpi` (append-only: exception, organization, transformation, `kpi_definition_id`, `linked_at`).

| `source_kind` | `failure_class` | Raised by | Organization |
